title: Matter, fields and the stress-energy tensor
scope: How matter and non-gravitational fields are described in relativity and why they gravitate. Starts from the continuum picture and rest-frame (MCRF) quantities: number density, number flux and particle conservation, energy density and its gamma-squared transformation. Builds the stress-energy tensor as a table of four-momentum fluxes, with its symmetry, the dust and perfect-fluid models, equations of state and the trace. Covers local energy-momentum conservation in flat and curved spacetime and its consequences: the relativistic Euler and energy equations, relativistic thermodynamics, adiabatic flow, geodesic motion of dust and the limits of global conservation. Includes Newtonian fluid mechanics as the limit, covariant electromagnetism with the Maxwell stress-energy tensor, scalar-field and vacuum stress-energy, the eigenframe classification and the energy conditions. Excludes the variational (Hilbert) definition of T, pressure as a source in the field equations, stellar and cosmological equations of state, and uses of energy conditions inside singularity theorems.

concepts.title: Continuum approximation and fluid elements
concepts.summary: Matter made of enormous numbers of particles is described by smooth fields such as density, velocity and pressure, obtained by averaging over fluid elements that are large compared with the particle spacing but small compared with the scale on which the averages change.
concepts.notes: The fluid element is idealized as a point once the averaging scale exists. In cosmology the same idea is applied with cells containing many galaxy clusters, which is what lets the universe be modelled as a homogeneous fluid.

concepts.title: Fluid
concepts.summary: A fluid is a continuum in which forces acting along the interface between neighbouring elements (shear) are weak compared with the normal push of pressure, so the material keeps deforming under any shear and flows.
concepts.notes: The boundary with solids is fuzzy: most solids flow under enough pressure. Rigidity is precisely the presence of strong tangential forces.

concepts.title: Momentarily comoving reference frame
aliases: rest frame of a fluid element
concepts.summary: The momentarily comoving reference frame (MCRF) of a particle or fluid element at an event is the inertial frame in which it is instantaneously at rest; every scalar property of a fluid (number density, energy density, pressure, temperature, entropy) is defined by its value measured there.
concepts.notes: The MCRF changes from element to element and from moment to moment; it is unique only up to spatial rotations, and its time basis vector is the four-velocity. In curved spacetime it becomes the local inertial frame comoving with the element. Defining fluid scalars in the MCRF is what makes them Lorentz scalars.

concepts.title: Four-velocity field of a flow
concepts.summary: A flow is described by a unit timelike vector field u whose value at each event is the four-velocity of the fluid element there; its integral curves (flow lines or streamlines) form a non-crossing congruence filling spacetime.

names: orthogonality of four-velocity and its gradient

merged_from: orthogonality of four-velocity and its gradient
concepts.notes: Because u.u = -1 everywhere, differentiating gives u_a u^a_{,b} = 0: the change of u in any direction is orthogonal to u. This identity is used repeatedly to simplify fluid equations. In Newtonian flow, streamlines coincide with particle paths only for steady flow.

concepts.title: Continuity equation
concepts.summary: A quantity is locally conserved when its density changes only by flow through the boundary: the time derivative of the density plus the divergence of its flux vanishes, which in four-vector form says the four-divergence of the current is zero.
concepts.notes: Integrating with the divergence theorem gives the integral form: the change of the enclosed amount equals minus the outward flux. Local conservation is stronger than global conservation, which would allow a quantity to vanish in one place and reappear far away; relativity rules that out because it would need faster-than-light transport. Applies to charge, particle number, rest mass and, row by row, to energy-momentum.

concepts.title: Pressure
concepts.summary: Pressure is the isotropic normal stress of a fluid: in the rest frame of an element it is the force per unit area across any surface, the same in every direction, and it equals the momentum flux carried across the surface by forces or by moving particles.

names: pressure as momentum flux from random motion

merged_from: pressure as momentum flux from random motion
concepts.notes: Any matter with random particle velocities has pressure, even a collisionless gas (radiation, a rarefied plasma, stars in a galaxy); if its velocity distribution is isotropic in the MCRF its stress-energy tensor has perfect-fluid form. Only matter with no random motion (dust) is pressureless. Do not confuse p with momentum.

concepts.title: Convective derivative
concepts.summary: The convective (material) derivative gives the rate of change of a quantity following a fluid element: the local rate of change at a fixed point plus the change due to being carried along the velocity, d/dt = partial_t + v.grad.
concepts.notes: Relativistically it is replaced by the covariant directional derivative along the fluid four-velocity, nabla_u.

concepts.title: Euler equation (Newtonian)
concepts.summary: Euler's equation is Newton's second law per unit volume for an inviscid fluid: mass density times convective acceleration equals minus the pressure gradient plus the gravitational (body) force density.

names: pressure force on a fluid element

merged_from: pressure force on a fluid element
concepts.notes: The pressure force on an element is minus the surface integral of p, which by the gradient theorem is minus the volume integral of grad p, so uniform pressure exerts no net force. In steady flow nothing changes at a fixed point and the convective derivative reduces to v.grad.

concepts.title: Hydrostatic equilibrium
concepts.summary: A fluid at rest in a gravitational field is in hydrostatic equilibrium when its pressure gradient exactly balances gravity, grad p = -rho grad Phi; for uniform density in uniform gravity pressure rises linearly with depth (Pascal's law).
concepts.notes: Relativistically the inertia and weight of the fluid involve rho + p, which leads to the relativistic hydrostatic equation of stellar structure.

concepts.title: Vorticity and irrotational flow
concepts.summary: Vorticity is the curl of a fluid velocity field and measures the local rotation of fluid elements; flow with zero vorticity is irrotational, and on a simply connected region its velocity is the gradient of a velocity potential.

concepts.title: Bernoulli's equation
concepts.summary: Bernoulli's equation expresses energy conservation for inviscid flow: for steady isentropic flow, v^2/2 plus the gravitational potential plus the specific enthalpy is constant along each streamline, and for irrotational flow a version holds throughout the fluid.
concepts.notes: Obtained by rewriting the (v.grad)v term of Euler with a vorticity identity and absorbing grad p / rho into the gradient of specific enthalpy when entropy is uniform. A relativistic steady-flow version exists (GA exercise 39.2).

concepts.title: Number density
concepts.summary: The number density n of a fluid is the number of particles per unit volume measured in the MCRF; an observer who sees the particles moving with speed v measures gamma n, because the box containing them is Lorentz contracted.
concepts.notes: In astrophysics n is usually taken as baryon number density, since baryons carry most of the mass and are conserved.

concepts.title: Number-flux four-vector
concepts.summary: The number-flux four-vector N = n u packages particle density and particle flux: its time component in any frame is the density measured there and its spatial components are the fluxes of particles across surfaces of constant x^i.

names: flux as contraction of one-form with vector

merged_from: flux as contraction of one-form with vector
concepts.notes: Density is itself a flux: the flux of world lines across a surface of constant time. The flux across any hypersurface is the contraction of N with the surface normal one-form. Multiplying by the particle rest mass gives the rest-mass current rho_0 u. Its conservation is the relativistic continuity equation.

concepts.title: Conservation of particle number
concepts.summary: If particles are neither created nor destroyed the number-flux vector is divergence-free, (n u^a)_{,a} = 0 in flat spacetime and (n u^a)_{;a} = 0 in curved spacetime; in practice this is applied to baryon number or rest mass.

names: conservation of particle number in curved spacetime

merged_from: conservation of particle number in curved spacetime
concepts.notes: Baryon number is conserved in all observed processes even when rest mass and particle identity change, so the assumption is hardly a restriction (proposed exceptions such as proton decay are irrelevant for most problems). Equivalently d(nV)/dtau = 0 for a comoving volume. With sqrt(-g) it reads d_a(sqrt(-g) n u^a) = 0.

concepts.title: Rest-mass density
aliases: total energy density versus rest-mass density
concepts.summary: The rest-mass density rho_0 = m n is the rest mass of the particles per unit volume in the MCRF; it differs from the total energy density rho, which also counts thermal, chemical and interaction energy, and the two coincide only for dust.

names: total energy density versus rest-mass density

merged_from: total energy density versus rest-mass density
concepts.notes: Common confusion: the rho in the perfect-fluid tensor is total energy density, not rest-mass density. Rest-mass density is the quantity closest to the Newtonian source of gravity, which relativity must replace.

concepts.title: Energy density of matter
concepts.summary: The energy density rho of a fluid is its total energy per unit volume measured in the MCRF, including rest mass plus internal energy (thermal, chemical, interaction), so rho = n(m + Pi) = rho_0(1 + epsilon).
concepts.notes: For dust with no internal energy rho = m n. For adiabatic flow the specific internal energy is a function of rho_0 alone and the first law gives p = rho_0^2 d(epsilon)/d(rho_0).

concepts.title: Gamma-squared transformation of energy density
concepts.summary: An observer who sees dust of rest-frame energy density rho moving at speed v measures energy density gamma^2 rho: one gamma from the larger energy of each particle and one from Lorentz contraction of the volume. Because two factors of gamma appear, energy density cannot be a component of a four-vector and needs a rank-2 tensor.

concepts.title: Stress-energy tensor
aliases: flux interpretation of the energy-momentum tensor
slot recipe for observer-measured energy and momentum
concepts.summary: The stress-energy tensor T is the symmetric rank-2 tensor whose component T^{ab} is the flux of the a-component of four-momentum across a surface of constant x^b: T^00 is energy density, T^0i energy flux, T^i0 momentum density and T^ij stress. It describes all non-gravitational matter and fields and is the source of gravity in general relativity.

names: flux interpretation of the energy-momentum tensor
orthonormal-frame components of the energy-momentum tensor
slot recipe for observer-measured energy and momentum
ad hoc construction of energy-momentum tensors

merged_from: flux interpretation of the energy-momentum tensor
orthonormal-frame components of the energy-momentum tensor
slot recipe for observer-measured energy and momentum
ad hoc construction of energy-momentum tensors
concepts.notes: Observer readings come from filling the slots: T(u,u) is the energy density measured by an observer with four-velocity u, -T^{a}_{b}u^b is the energy-flux (energy current) vector that observer sees, and feeding a unit spatial vector in the other slot picks out momentum density or stress. Matter fields means every non-gravitational field, massive or massless. Stress-energy tensors of simple models are often built ad hoc: write the most general tensor from the available fields and fix coefficients by demanding that conservation reproduces known non-relativistic physics. The variational (Hilbert) definition belongs to action-principles-and-field-theory.

concepts.title: Stress tensor
concepts.summary: The spatial block T^ij of the stress-energy tensor is the stress tensor: the flux of i-momentum across a surface with normal along j, equivalently the i-component of force per unit area exerted across that surface, with normal stresses (pressures) on the diagonal and shear stresses off it.

concepts.title: Symmetry of the stress-energy tensor
aliases: equality of energy flux and momentum density
concepts.summary: The stress-energy tensor is symmetric, T^{ab} = T^{ba}: in the MCRF T^{0i} = T^{i0} because energy flux and momentum density are the same thing when energy is inertia, and T^{ij} = T^{ji} because otherwise small elements would suffer unbounded angular acceleration.

names: equality of energy flux and momentum density
symmetry of the energy-momentum tensor and angular momentum conservation

merged_from: symmetry of the energy-momentum tensor and angular momentum conservation
equality of energy flux and momentum density
concepts.notes: Symmetry in one frame implies symmetry in all frames. In field theory, symmetry of T is equivalent to conservation of the angular-momentum flux built from x^a T^{bc}; the canonical Noether tensor is generally not symmetric, which is one reason the Hilbert tensor is used as the gravitational source.

concepts.title: Dust
concepts.summary: Dust is matter whose particles share one velocity at each event and do not interact, so it has no pressure or other stress; its stress-energy tensor is T = rho u (x) u, the outer product of the momentum carried per particle with the number-flux vector.

names: dust energy-momentum tensor as an outer product
energy-momentum tensor of a moving dust swarm

merged_from: dust energy-momentum tensor as an outer product
energy-momentum tensor of a moving dust swarm
concepts.notes: In a frame where the dust moves, the components are rho gamma^2 (energy density), rho gamma^2 v^i (energy flux and momentum density) and rho gamma^2 v^i v^j (momentum flux). It is the p = 0 perfect fluid and the standard model of matter in the present universe, where pressure is negligible against rest-mass energy.

concepts.title: Point-particle stress-energy tensor
aliases: world-line delta-function representation of a point particle
concepts.summary: A point particle of mass m on world line z(tau) can be treated with field tools by writing its densities as proper-time integrals of a four-dimensional delta function, giving T^{ab}(x) = m integral of u^a u^b delta^4(x - z(tau)) dtau, which is nonzero only on the world line.

names: world-line delta-function representation of a point particle

merged_from: world-line delta-function representation of a point particle
concepts.notes: Integrating over coordinate time leaves a three-dimensional delta function at the particle position divided by u^0, the origin of gamma factors in lab-frame densities.

concepts.title: Local conservation of energy-momentum
concepts.summary: In special relativity the stress-energy tensor of any closed system is divergence-free, T^{ab}_{,b} = 0: in every inertial frame the rate of change of the density of each four-momentum component is balanced by the divergence of its flux.

names: local conservation of energy-momentum in flat spacetime

merged_from: local conservation of energy-momentum in flat spacetime
concepts.notes: The b-sum over one index is a separate continuity equation for each a: a = 0 gives energy conservation and a = i gives momentum conservation, i.e. the equations of motion of the matter. Derived by energy bookkeeping on a small cube. For dust it reproduces continuity and the force-free Euler equation.

concepts.title: Viscosity and heat conduction
concepts.summary: Viscosity is the tangential force between neighbouring fluid elements and appears as off-diagonal stresses T^{ij} in the MCRF, while heat conduction is energy transport without bulk motion and appears as nonzero T^{0i} (and T^{i0}) there; their absence defines a perfect fluid.
concepts.notes: A consistent, causal and stable theory of relativistic dissipative fluids is subtle and needs second-order theories such as Israel-Stewart; the three books only flag this.

concepts.title: Perfect fluid
concepts.summary: A perfect fluid has no viscosity and no heat conduction in the rest frame of each element, so it is fully described by its energy density rho, isotropic pressure p and four-velocity u; it is the relativistic generalization of an ideal inviscid fluid.
concepts.notes: With no dissipation, entropy is not produced. Dust is the p = 0 case. GA ch40 also recasts the perfect fluid as a field theory (rest-mass density plus flow-line congruence) with Lagrangian -rho; that variational treatment belongs to action-principles-and-field-theory.

concepts.title: Perfect-fluid stress-energy tensor
aliases: T = (rho + p) u u + p g
concepts.summary: The stress-energy tensor of a perfect fluid is T^{ab} = (rho + p) u^a u^b + p g^{ab} (signature -+++), which is diag(rho, p, p, p) in the fluid rest frame; it is found by writing the rest-frame matrix and recognizing a tensor expression that reproduces it.

names: energy-momentum tensor of a perfect fluid
perfect-fluid energy-momentum tensor in an orthonormal frame

merged_from: energy-momentum tensor of a perfect fluid
perfect-fluid energy-momentum tensor in an orthonormal frame
concepts.notes: Examples: in an orthonormal frame the rest-frame form is always diag(rho, p, p, p); for a static fluid in a static metric only u^0 = (-g_00)^{-1/2} is nonzero. In curved spacetime eta is replaced by g (comma-goes-to-semicolon reasoning). With signature +--- (d'Inverno) the pressure term has the opposite sign. The form is confirmed by the Hilbert variation of the fluid action.

concepts.title: Trace of the stress-energy tensor
concepts.summary: The trace T = g_{ab} T^{ab} is a scalar; for a perfect fluid it equals -rho + 3p (signature -+++), so it is -rho for dust and vanishes for radiation and for the electromagnetic field.

names: traceless energy-momentum tensor and massless fields

merged_from: traceless energy-momentum tensor and massless fields
concepts.notes: A vanishing trace is associated with massless quanta and scale invariance (photons, the Maxwell field). The trace appears in the trace-reversed field equations and is the spin-0 part of T in graviton coupling.

concepts.title: Projection tensor orthogonal to the four-velocity
concepts.summary: For a unit timelike vector u the tensor h_{ab} = g_{ab} + u_a u_b removes the component of any vector along u, leaves vectors orthogonal to u unchanged, and acts as the spatial metric of the local rest space of that observer; its trace is 3.
concepts.notes: Generalizes to any non-null vector q by dividing q_a q_b by q.q; null vectors fail. Used to split fluid conservation laws into energy and momentum parts, to decompose velocity gradients into expansion, shear and rotation, and in covariant forms of Newton-like force laws. In the fluid perfect-fluid tensor, p multiplies exactly this projector.

concepts.title: Equation of state
aliases: pressure from an equation of state
concepts.summary: An equation of state is the relation fixed by microphysics that gives a fluid pressure in terms of other state variables, p = p(rho, S) or p = p(n, T), reducing to a barotropic p = p(rho) when entropy or temperature is uniform; it closes the fluid equations.

names: pressure from an equation of state

merged_from: pressure from an equation of state
concepts.notes: For a simple fluid in local equilibrium any two state variables fix the rest. Given rho(n, s), the first law gives p = n (d rho / d n)_s - rho. Standard cases: dust p = 0, radiation p = rho/3, stiff fluid p = rho (sound speed equal to c), vacuum p = -rho. Stellar equations of state (polytropes, degenerate matter) belong to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars; the cosmic w parameter to cosmological-dynamics.

concepts.title: Radiation equation of state
concepts.summary: A gas of photons or of any ultra-relativistic particles has pressure equal to one third of its energy density, p = rho/3, which is exactly the condition that its stress-energy tensor be traceless.

names: ultrarelativistic equation of state p = rho/3

merged_from: ultrarelativistic equation of state p = rho/3
concepts.notes: Follows from kinetic theory of an isotropic collisionless gas of massless particles or from the photon partition function, and also as the high-momentum limit of a degenerate Fermi gas, where rest mass becomes negligible (relevant for neutron-star cores).

concepts.title: Relativistic first law of thermodynamics
aliases: first law for a fluid element
concepts.summary: For a fluid element with a fixed number of particles, energy conservation in the MCRF reads d rho = ((rho + p)/n) dn + n T ds, where s is entropy per particle; the combination rho + p appears because compressing the element does p dV work.

names: first law of thermodynamics per unit mass
first law of thermodynamics for a fluid element
temperature and specific entropy via integrating factor

merged_from: first law of thermodynamics for a fluid element
first law of thermodynamics per unit mass
temperature and specific entropy via integrating factor
concepts.notes: Derived from dE = T dS - p dV with V = N/n and E = rho V. Schutz introduces T and specific entropy as an integrating factor of d rho - (rho + p) dn/n. The Newtonian per-unit-mass version is d(epsilon) = T ds - p d(1/rho_0), and the specific enthalpy h = epsilon + p/rho_0 satisfies dh = T ds + dp/rho_0.

concepts.title: Relativistic Euler equation
aliases: relativistic equation of motion of a perfect fluid
concepts.summary: The part of the conservation law of a perfect fluid orthogonal to u gives (rho + p) nabla_u u^a = -h^{ab} partial_b p: fluid elements accelerate down the pressure gradient measured in their rest space, with rho + p as the inertia.
concepts.notes: In the MCRF of flat spacetime it reads (rho + p) a_i + p_{,i} = 0, compared with rho a + grad p = 0. Consequence: fluid elements follow geodesics only where the projected pressure gradient vanishes, so only pressureless dust (or constant pressure) moves geodesically.

concepts.title: Inertial mass density rho + p
aliases: inertial mass density of a fluid
concepts.summary: In relativistic fluid dynamics the resistance of a fluid element to acceleration is measured by rho + p, not rho: pressure contributes to inertia, which matters when pressure is comparable to energy density.
concepts.notes: Together with pressure being a source of gravity, this is why relativistic stars need steeper pressure gradients than Newtonian ones. rho + p is the relativistic enthalpy density.

concepts.title: Energy equation for a perfect fluid
aliases: projection of the conservation law along the 4-velocity
concepts.summary: Contracting the conservation law of a perfect fluid with u gives the energy equation d rho/d tau = -(rho + p) nabla.u: the energy density following a fluid element falls both by dilution as the element expands and by the p dV work its pressure does.

names: projection of the conservation law along the 4-velocity

merged_from: projection of the conservation law along the 4-velocity
concepts.notes: The divergence of u is the fractional rate of change of the comoving volume per unit proper time, nabla.u = (1/V) dV/dtau. Combined with particle conservation it reads d rho/dtau = ((rho + p)/n) dn/dtau. Its cosmological specialization is the fluid equation of Friedmann models.

concepts.title: Adiabatic flow of a perfect fluid
concepts.summary: Comparing the energy equation of a particle-conserving perfect fluid with the first law shows that each element keeps its entropy per particle, u^a s_{,a} = ds/dtau = 0: perfect-fluid flow is adiabatic (isentropic along flow lines).
concepts.notes: Because s is a scalar the law is unchanged in curved spacetime. With heat flow allowed, the second law only gives ds/dtau >= 0. Uniform-entropy (isentropic everywhere) flow additionally has grad s = 0.

concepts.title: Relativistic speed of sound
concepts.summary: Small adiabatic disturbances of a fluid travel at the sound speed c_s given by c_s^2 = (dp/d rho) at fixed entropy; linearizing particle conservation and the relativistic Euler equation about a static background gives a wave equation with this speed.
concepts.notes: Causality requires c_s <= 1, which a stiff fluid (p = rho) saturates; radiation has c_s^2 = 1/3.

concepts.title: Newtonian limit of relativistic fluid dynamics
aliases: non-relativistic limit of the fluid stress tensor
concepts.summary: When bulk speeds are small, pressure is small compared with energy density (p << rho c^2) and gravity is weak, the relativistic conservation laws reduce to the Newtonian continuity and Euler equations, and the stress-energy tensor is dominated by T^00 = rho c^2.

names: Newtonian limit of a perfect fluid
non-relativistic limit of the fluid stress tensor

merged_from: Newtonian limit of a perfect fluid
non-relativistic limit of the fluid stress tensor
concepts.notes: Nonrelativistic matter needs small random velocities as well as small bulk velocities, since pressure is of order rho v^2. In the weak-field metric the spatial conservation equations give Euler with a gravitational force and grad p + rho grad phi = 0 for a static fluid.

concepts.title: Covariant conservation of energy-momentum
concepts.summary: In curved spacetime local energy-momentum conservation becomes nabla_b T^{ab} = 0: it holds in every local inertial frame, contains the equations of motion of matter, and is guaranteed by the field equations through the contracted Bianchi identity.

names: covariant conservation law for the energy-momentum tensor

merged_from: covariant conservation law for the energy-momentum tensor
concepts.notes: Obtained by writing the flat law in a local inertial frame and replacing commas with semicolons (minimal coupling). Because it must hold for any metric, it demands a divergence-free geometric side, which selects the Einstein tensor over the Ricci tensor. It does not by itself give globally conserved totals. It can also be derived from diffeomorphism invariance of the matter action (action-principles-and-field-theory).

concepts.title: Geodesic motion of dust
concepts.summary: For dust, covariant conservation of T splits into rest-mass conservation along u and u^b nabla_b u^a = 0 orthogonal to it, so dust particles follow timelike geodesics; more generally a small body exchanging no energy-momentum with its surroundings moves on a geodesic.
concepts.notes: This shows that in general relativity the equations of motion of matter follow from the field equations rather than being postulated separately. Rigorous point-particle versions need an energy condition (Ehlers-Geroch). Fluids with pressure gradients do not move geodesically.

concepts.title: Global conservation laws for matter in curved spacetime
aliases: non-existence of global energy conservation in curved spacetime
concepts.summary: Covariant conservation of T gives a conserved total energy or momentum of matter only when the spacetime has a corresponding symmetry (a Killing vector); in a generic curved spacetime matter and gravity exchange energy and there is no global conservation law for matter alone.

names: non-existence of global energy conservation in curved spacetime

merged_from: non-existence of global energy conservation in curved spacetime
concepts.notes: If the metric is independent of x^mu, (sqrt(-g) T^nu_mu)_{,nu} = 0 is an ordinary divergence and the integral of sqrt(-g) T^0_mu over a slice is constant for bounded matter; with azimuthal symmetry this gives total angular momentum. The reason is that nabla_b T^{ab} = 0 is not an ordinary divergence of a vector, and parallel transport is path dependent.

concepts.title: Four-current
concepts.summary: The four-current J^a = (rho, j) combines the charge density and current density of electromagnetism (or of any conserved scalar quantity) into one four-vector; it sources the electromagnetic field and local charge conservation is d_a J^a = 0.
concepts.notes: The flux of J through a hypersurface element J^a dSigma_a gives the charge in a spatial slice or crossing a timelike wall.

concepts.title: Faraday tensor
concepts.summary: The Faraday (electromagnetic field) tensor F_{ab} is an antisymmetric rank-2 tensor whose time-space components are the electric field and space-space components the magnetic field; E and B therefore mix under Lorentz transformations as parts of one object.

names: antisymmetry of F and conservation of rest mass

merged_from: antisymmetry of F and conservation of rest mass
concepts.notes: In terms of the four-potential F_{ab} = partial_a A_b - partial_b A_a (sign and index conventions differ between books). It has six independent components. Its form-language version F = dA belongs to differential-forms-and-frames.

concepts.title: Electromagnetic four-potential
concepts.summary: The four-potential A_a combines the scalar and vector potentials into a one-form field whose antisymmetrized derivatives give the Faraday tensor; it is defined only up to adding the gradient of a scalar (a gauge transformation).
concepts.notes: Writing F in terms of A makes the homogeneous Maxwell equations identities. It is the middle rung of the analogy scalar wave, electromagnetic wave, gravitational wave (metric perturbation).

concepts.title: Maxwell equations in tensor form
concepts.summary: In special relativity Maxwell's equations become d_b F^{ab} = J^a (Gauss and Ampere-Maxwell laws) and d_{[a} F_{bc]} = 0 (no monopoles and Faraday's law), manifestly Lorentz covariant once E, B, rho and j are assumed to transform as parts of F and J.

names: inhomogeneous Maxwell equations in tensor form

merged_from: inhomogeneous Maxwell equations in tensor form
concepts.notes: Charge conservation follows from the antisymmetry of F. Historically, requiring Maxwell theory to be Lorentz covariant drove the discovery of special relativity; the tensor character of F is a hypothesis confirmed by experiment.

concepts.title: Maxwell equations in curved spacetime
aliases: covariant Maxwell equations in curved spacetime
concepts.summary: By minimal coupling, Maxwell's equations in curved spacetime are nabla_b F^{ab} = J^a and partial_{[a} F_{bc]} = 0; the second may keep partial derivatives because the symmetric connection terms cancel under antisymmetrization.
concepts.notes: The divergence can be evaluated as (1/sqrt(-g)) partial_b (sqrt(-g) F^{ab}), which reduces the charged-black-hole problem to a single ODE for a radial field. Together with the Einstein equation sourced by the Maxwell stress-energy tensor they form the Einstein-Maxwell system.

concepts.title: Maxwell stress-energy tensor
concepts.summary: The electromagnetic field carries stress-energy T^{ab} = F^{ac} F^b_c - (1/4) g^{ab} F_{cd} F^{cd} (Heaviside-Lorentz units, signature -+++): its time-time part is the field energy density, time-space part the Poynting flux, and space-space part minus the Maxwell stress. It is symmetric, traceless, and divergence-free when the source-free Maxwell equations hold.
concepts.notes: Normalizations differ: in Gaussian units there is an overall 1/4 pi and energy density (E^2 + B^2)/8 pi. Tracelessness in four dimensions means that in electrovac regions the Einstein equation reduces to R_ab = 8 pi T_ab. With sources, the divergence equals minus the Lorentz force density on the charges. Derivable by metric variation of the Maxwell Lagrangian or by symmetrizing the canonical tensor.

concepts.title: Superposition of stress-energy tensors
concepts.summary: The stress-energy tensor of several non-interacting components is the sum of their separate tensors; for interacting components only the total is conserved, and the exchange between them expresses their mutual forces.
concepts.notes: Example: charged dust, T = T_dust + T_Maxwell. Conservation of the sum yields energy conservation and the Lorentz-force equation of motion for the charged particles.

concepts.title: Stress-energy tensor of a scalar field
aliases: energy-momentum tensor of a complex scalar field
concepts.summary: A real scalar field with potential V has T_{ab} = partial_a phi partial_b phi - g_{ab}[(1/2) g^{cd} partial_c phi partial_d phi + V(phi)]; in flat space its energy density (1/2) phi-dot^2 + (1/2)|grad phi|^2 + V is positive for V >= 0.

names: energy-momentum tensor of a scalar field
energy-momentum tensor of a scalar field
energy-momentum tensor of a complex scalar field

merged_from: energy-momentum tensor of a scalar field
energy-momentum tensor of a complex scalar field
concepts.notes: For a massive Klein-Gordon field V = m^2 phi^2 / 2. It follows from the Hilbert prescription applied to the scalar Lagrangian (action-principles-and-field-theory); the complex-field version is analogous.

concepts.title: Energy density and pressure of a homogeneous scalar field
aliases: scalar field as a perfect fluid
concepts.summary: A spatially uniform scalar field behaves as a perfect fluid with rho = phi-dot^2/2 + V and p = phi-dot^2/2 - V: kinetic energy adds to both, while potential energy adds to density but subtracts from pressure, so a potential-dominated field has p close to -rho.

names: energy density and pressure of a homogeneous scalar field

merged_from: energy density and pressure of a homogeneous scalar field
concepts.notes: This is the basis of inflaton and quintessence models (physical-cosmology).

concepts.title: Vacuum stress-energy tensor
concepts.summary: Vacuum energy has stress-energy tensor T^vac_{ab} = -rho_vac g_{ab}, the only form that looks the same to every observer; it is a perfect fluid with p = -rho, and moving a cosmological-constant term to the source side gives exactly this with rho_vac = Lambda/(8 pi G).
concepts.notes: Its role in the expansion (negative pressure, repulsive rho + 3p, no dilution) belongs to cosmological-dynamics; the vacuum-energy problem to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

concepts.title: Null dust
concepts.summary: Null dust is incoherent radiation modelled by a dust-like stress-energy tensor T^{ab} = rho k^a k^b with a null vector k in place of the timelike four-velocity; it describes streams of massless particles all moving in one direction at light speed.
concepts.notes: Appears as a source in Vaidya and colliding plane-wave spacetimes.

concepts.title: Eigenframe classification of the stress-energy tensor
concepts.summary: Solving the eigenvalue problem T^a_b v^b = lambda v^a for ordinary matter gives one timelike and three spacelike eigenvectors; in that orthonormal frame T is diagonal with the energy density as one eigenvalue and the principal stresses p_1, p_2, p_3 as the others.

names: eigenvalue problem for the energy-momentum tensor

merged_from: eigenvalue problem for the energy-momentum tensor
concepts.notes: The timelike eigenvector defines the rest frame (four-velocity) of the medium. Equal principal stresses give a perfect fluid; zero stresses give dust. Other Hawking-Ellis types (with null eigenvectors, such as null dust) exist. Energy conditions are conveniently written in terms of these eigenvalues.

concepts.title: Energy conditions
concepts.summary: Energy conditions are inequalities on the stress-energy tensor, such as non-negative energy density for every observer or causal energy flow, that express what physically reasonable matter should satisfy; they are the matter inputs to focusing and singularity theorems.
concepts.notes: Inventing a metric and reading off T from the Einstein equation usually yields matter violating them, which is why that approach is rarely useful. Quantum fields and strong fields can violate them.

concepts.title: Weak energy condition
concepts.summary: The weak energy condition requires every observer to measure non-negative energy density, T_{ab} v^a v^b >= 0 for all timelike v; for a perfect fluid it means rho >= 0 and rho + p >= 0.
concepts.notes: By continuity it implies the null energy condition T_ab k^a k^b >= 0, which feeds the null convergence condition. It says nothing about energy flux.

concepts.title: Dominant energy condition
concepts.summary: The dominant energy condition requires every observer to measure non-negative energy density and a causal (timelike or null) energy flux, so energy never flows faster than light; for a perfect fluid it means rho >= |p|.
concepts.notes: In the eigenframe: mu >= 0 and |p_alpha| <= mu, no principal stress exceeds the energy density.

concepts.title: Strong energy condition
concepts.summary: The strong energy condition requires (T_{ab} - (1/2) T g_{ab}) v^a v^b >= 0 for all timelike v, which through the Einstein equation is R_{ab} v^a v^b >= 0; for a perfect fluid it means rho + 3p >= 0 and rho + p >= 0, i.e. gravity is attractive for timelike geodesics.
concepts.notes: Despite the name it does not imply the weak condition. A positive cosmological constant or a potential-dominated scalar field violates it, which is how accelerated expansion is possible.
